source: Sulla S, in un'ora di traffico. Un tipo di circa ventisei anni, cappello floscio con una cordicella al posto del nastro, collo troppo lungo, come se glielo avessero tirato. La gente scende. Il tizio in questione si arrabbia con un vicino. Gli rimprovera di spingerlo ogni volta che passa qualcuno. Tono lamentoso, con pretese di cattiveria. Non appena vede un posto libero, vi si butta. Due ore più tardi lo incontro alla Cour de Rome, davanti alla Gare Saint-Lazare. È con un amico che gli dice: «Dovresti far mettere un bottone in più al soprabito». Gli fa vedere dove (alla sciancratura) e perché.

gens.text: An aviation security check-in station was bustling at the busiest hour. The lines were thick, the barriers high up, and the belongings were meticulously separated into trays. A lone officer stood among the crowd, his expression unreadable. He scanned their every inch, their bags, their shoes, and even their cell phones—every single piece of luggage they held. As he surveyed them, an officer and a traveler were lined up side by side on a queue. Their faces showed signs of apprehension and confusion. They were wearing masks, but their intentions were clear—they wanted to enter the country. The officer, who appeared slightly perplexed, began to explain the procedures to the traveler. "This is my duty, my fellow travelers," the officer said, gesturing toward the scanner, metal detector, and the body-scan device. They were waiting patiently, their hands folded over their hearts, ready to comply. After several minutes, the officer announced a series of questions and requests from the airline. The traveler had already been fingerprinted and his passport checked against a database; he could proceed without further issues. The officer nodded approvingly and handed him the boarding pass. He stepped through the security gate, and the line moved forward. As the officer passed by, the traveler waved, smiling at the officer. They exchanged pleasantries before the flight crew took off to the next stop. In the aftermath, the traveler left the station feeling relieved, but the sight of the officer and the crowd still lingered in his mind.
